text:
cs_julia: FYI, ACME (customer) just escalated — seeing a spike of 401s + 502s since ~09:10Z. They say traffic is being routed to us-east even though their org is pinned to eu-west. Customer reports latency 2-3x and an unexpected billing jump. attaching minimal repro below

ops_bot: alert: route-failover-policy triggered for org=acme, eu-west -> fallback us-east after 5m of degraded responses (error_rate 18%)

eng_oncall_tom: can someone grab a sample req id / traceID and a curl repro? also need to know if this is new rollout of routing nor changes to auth signing keys.

cs_julia: repro (from customer's side):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \\
  -H "X-User-Region: eu-west-1" \\
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
response headers: `X-Served-Region: us-east-1`, status `401`

logs (customer-provided):
```
resp: 401 Unauthorized
X-Served-Region: us-east-1
X-Auth-Error: token_region_mismatch
```

infra_elaine: fyi I pushed a change to the global routing policy earlier today to make fallback more permissive for high-throughput customers — motive was to reduce queueing. That added `regionalFallback: global` for some org groups. I'm worried that for orgs using region-bound tokens this will cause token validation failures.

raj: confirmed — routing config change at 08:55Z. New behavior: if eu-west instance reports degraded, route engine will pick nearest available global pool (us-east) without rewriting the auth-context. Tokens are region-bound so we get token validation mismatches.

eng_oncall_tom: ok mitigation suggestion: 1) pin org=acme to eu-west 2) disable the new permissive fallback for org-groups with region-bound tokens. Can infra/raj do the pin now?

raj: running pin now. command: `redwood route pin --org acme --region eu-west-1 --scope org`

deploy_bot: config-change: route-pin applied for org=acme by raj @ 09:27Z (conf: pin-eu-west-org)

eng_oncall_tom: cs_julia, can you ask ACME to retry a request and paste trace id if they have it? also I'll watch metrics.

cs_julia: they retried — trace id `tr-0a3f2b`. here's customer curl again; got 200 and `X-Served-Region: eu-west-1` now. they confirm latency back to normal. :relieved:

mike: billing note — we saw a small cross-region egress/compute spike while the fallback served requests from us-east. I'll flag billing for credit review and start a quick usage spike analysis for acme (09:10–09:30Z).

eng_oncall_tom: root cause (short): permissive fallback policy introduced 08:55Z routed eu-west traffic to global pools (us-east) without region auth rewrite; region-bound tokens then fail validation causing 401s and fallback loops; when retries hit global pool they either failed or succeeded but with high latency and extra egress.

infra_elaine: immediate followups done: reverted permissive fallback for org-groups with region-bound tokens at 09:20Z; added temporary allowlist to avoid global fallback for pinned orgs.

sylvia: customer comms drafted: "We've applied an emergency route pin for your org and reverted the fallback change; we're investigating and will follow up with a root cause and credit. Apologies for the disruption." Want engineering approval before I send.

eng_oncall_tom: send it. include a note we're doing a postmortem and will propose remediation + credits.

ops_bot: note: alert cleared for org=acme at 09:30Z (error_rate < 1%)

mike: billing spike estimate preliminary: ~1.9k USD extra egress/compute for acme — will confirm. recommending credit.

eng_oncall_tom: quick timeline for postmortem doc (owners):
- infra_elaine: fix routing policy to be region-aware by default + add config guardrails (owner: infra)
- raj: add automation tests to simulate region token mismatch in staging (owner: routing)
- eng_oncall_tom: add metric & alert for `token_region_mismatch` and `served_region != requested_region` for orgs pinned to a region
- devex/sylvia: customer comms and credit workflow (owner: support)

infra_elaine: plan: change default to `regionalFallback: disabled` for orgs with region-locked tokens, add lint rule in deployment pipeline to prevent unguarded flips, and add a canary check that attempts a signed request rewrite. Target PR by EOD.

raj: test plan: inject failure in eu-west staging, assert routing engine prefers local pool or returns explicit 5xx instead of cross-region failover; add to release gating.

eng_oncall_tom: temporary post-incident ops notes: 1) if you see token_region_mismatch spike, pin affected orgs, 2) revert permissive fallbacks, 3) notify billing for credits. I'll kick off a postmortem doc and add timeline + severity + impact numbers.

sylvia: sent ACME update at 09:40Z. they replied: "Thanks — please keep us posted on credits. Our SLAs were affected."

mike: tagging billing team: @billing — acme likely needs credit for cross-region egress costs; please triage. (reacted :eyes:)

eng_oncall_tom: thanks all. action items captured. I'll create the postmortem draft and link here. :thumbsup:
